title: DepState-JEPA: Learning Depth-Grounded State Representation for Visual Perception and Manipulation

problem.summary: Our intuition is that understanding what an action will change starts with understanding where things are: complementary RGB and depth observations ground a common scene representation from which to infer those changes.
statements: Our intuition is that understanding what an action will change starts with understanding where things are: complementary RGB and depth observations ground a common scene representation from which to infer those changes.

Guided by this intuition, we introduce DepState-JEPA, a dual-stream RGB-Depth joint-embedding predictive architecture that connects spatial understanding with action-conditioned prediction through a shared latent state, DepState.

evidence.quote: Our intuition is that understanding what an action will change starts with understanding where things are: complementary RGB and depth observations ground a common scene representation from which to infer those changes.

Guided by this intuition, we introduce DepState-JEPA, a dual-stream RGB-Depth joint-embedding predictive architecture that connects spatial understanding with action-conditioned prediction through a shared latent state, DepState.

background.summary: Built on V-JEPA 2.1, the framework uses depth both as a complementary observation stream and to ground both modalities in metric 3D space, aggregating shared information into DepState while retaining modality-private features for decoding.

evidence.quote: Built on V-JEPA 2.1, the framework uses depth both as a complementary observation stream and to ground both modalities in metric 3D space, aggregating shared information into DepState while retaining modality-private features for decoding.

Ray-conditioned readouts predict local features without target depth; after an action-conditioned transition, the same decoders predict future RGB and depth features using the predicted state and fixed initial private features.

components: For manipulation in real-world space, this requires relating the current spatial arrangement to the changes an action may cause.
Consider a robot reaching for a cup: RGB reveals its appearance and context, while depth locates the cup and gripper relative to the table in threedimensional space.
Anticipating the reach then requires reasoning about how this arrangement will change, not merely recognizing the cup.

experiments.summary: Locate 3D's 3D-JEPA predicts masked pointcloud features enriched by lifted 2D features, rather than maintaining separate RGB-depth streams (Arnaud et al., 2025); JEPADepth predicts depth from RGB with auxiliary latent supervision, rather than encoding measured depth (Grigore & Popa, 2026).

evidence.quote: Locate 3D's 3D-JEPA predicts masked pointcloud features enriched by lifted 2D features, rather than maintaining separate RGB-depth streams (Arnaud et al., 2025); JEPADepth predicts depth from RGB with auxiliary latent supervision, rather than encoding measured depth (Grigore & Popa, 2026).
These designs target multimodal perception or geometric estimation, but do not establish a common state interface between spatial understanding and action-driven evolution.
